name: Wachovia and the Mexican casas de cambio
scale: At least $373B in wires from Mexican currency exchange houses, over $420B in transactions not effectively monitored
outcome: $160M in 2010 ($110M forfeiture plus $50M OCC penalty), deferred prosecution
control_failed: Correspondent flows from foreign money service businesses never compared to what those businesses could plausibly earn

name: HSBC and the Sinaloa and Norte del Valle cartels
sector: Global bank, US and Mexico units
scale: At least $881M in drug proceeds laundered, $670B in HSBC Mexico wires and $9.4B in US dollar purchases left unmonitored
outcome: About $1.9B in forfeiture and penalties in 2012, deferred prosecution
control_failed: Mexico sat in the lowest risk tier, so bulk cash far above any customer profile went unreviewed

name: Danske Bank Estonia branch
scale: About EUR 200B in non resident flows, $160B of it routed through US banks
outcome: Guilty plea to conspiracy to commit bank fraud in 2022, about $2B forfeited
control_failed: Non resident accounts moved money in and straight back out, and the branch ran on a separate IT system head office did not monitor

name: 1MDB, Malaysia's sovereign fund
scale: About $4.5B misappropriated, per the US Department of Justice
outcome: Goldman Sachs paid about $2.9B in a 2020 global resolution, former prime minister Najib Razak convicted in 2020
control_failed: Bond proceeds hopped through offshore shells and ended in art, property and a superyacht without anyone asking who the shells were

name: Bank of Credit and Commerce International
scale: Billions for cartels and corrupt officials, never fully quantified
outcome: Shut down by regulators in several countries in July 1991
control_failed: Incorporated in Luxembourg, run from London, booked through the Cayman Islands, so no single supervisor ever saw the whole bank

name: Nauru's offshore banking sector
scale: An estimated $70B of Russian money in 1998, by a widely cited Russian central bank figure
outcome: US Treasury Section 311 designation in 2002, removed from the FATF blacklist in 2005 after new AML laws
control_failed: Hundreds of shell banks licensed from a single address with no supervision behind them

name: Al Capone and cash fronts
scale: Unknown, the cash was never on paper
outcome: Convicted of tax evasion in 1931, eleven year sentence
control_failed: Nothing compared a cash business's takings with similar businesses on the same street

name: TD Bank
scale: 92% of transaction volume, about $18.3T, unmonitored from 2018 to 2024, more than $670M moved by three laundering networks
outcome: Guilty plea in October 2024, about $3B in combined penalties, OCC asset cap
control_failed: Whole channels such as ACH and checks were excluded from automated monitoring, and the rule set stayed static for years

name: Las Vegas Strip casinos and an illegal bookmaker
scale: One illegal bookmaker gambled millions across three operators for years
outcome: About $26.8M in Nevada fines in 2025 (Resorts World $10.5M, MGM $8.5M, Caesars $7.8M)
control_failed: Player play was never tested against a credible source of funds
